title: Prove the compact embedding construction
promptMarkdown: Starting with a compact smooth manifold and a finite chart cover, reconstruct the map $F$ in the lesson and prove it is a smooth embedding. Your account must justify zero extension, injectivity, immersion, and the inverse topology separately. State why the argument neither proves the bound $2n$ nor immediately applies to a noncompact manifold. Illustrate the conclusion by an explicit embedding of $S^1$.
hintLadder: Keep the weights themselves as coordinates.
In the differential calculation, use the scalar components first.
Use compactness only after you have injectivity and immersion.
